items.title: Lam Research Sinks 16%, Applied Materials 15% in a Week. Lam Responds With $25 Billion Buyback
items.summary: Key TakeawaysLam Research (LRCX) fell approximately 16% during the week ended November 6, while Applied Materials (AMAT) declined roughly 15% as concerns about semiconductor spending pressured equipment stocks. Lam announced a $25 billion share repurchase authorization following the November 5 selloff, equivalent to approximately 10% of its market capitalization at the time.

items.title: Semiconductor equipment stocks: fundamentals, fair value, and the top pick
items.summary: Investing.com -- Wafer fab equipment (WFE) names are rallying today after a sharp slide. Applied Materials (AMAT) is $396.56 (+6.45%) and Lam Research (LRCX) is $237.68 (+6.87%). KLA (KLAC) is $161.68 (+5.68%) and ASML ADR (ASML) is $1,542.41 (+2.29%). All prices are as of Nov 11, 2026, 3:26 PM EST.

items.title: 13 Big Funds Sold Applied Materials. Should You Follow Them Before Earnings?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysThirteen big funds held fewer Applied Materials shares on June 30 than at the end of March, and four of them sold every share, according to their latest 13F filings. Several of the sellers added Lam Research, KLA or Teradyne in the same quarter.

items.title: Lam Research (LRCX) Just Gave Investors Something To Think About
items.summary: Lam Research (LRCX) has been in focus after its board approved a share repurchase program of up to US$25b with no termination date, along with a reaffirmed quarterly dividend of US$0.33 per share. Lam Research has been volatile in recent months, with the share price falling 28.16% over the past 30 days and 34.01% over 90 days. items.title: Applied Materials Rallies 8% Ahead of Earnings as Chip Stocks Rebound; Lam Research Jumps 9%, KLA Climbs 7%
items.summary: Chip equipment stocks are snapping back from a brutal month just as Applied Materials prepares to report. A cautious look at China and AI order strength could decide whether this bounce holds or fades.

items.title: Wall Street is cooling on Jensen Huang's Nvidia — but history says don't give up on the stock just yet
items.summary: Morgan Stanley and Bank of America pulled Nvidia from their best-ideas lists, but nearly all analysts still rate the stock a Buy.

items.title: Applied Materials Is Up 59% in a Year, Even After Halving From Its High: “Double Our Output”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysApplied Materials stock is up 59% over the past year, even after losing about half its value since its June 30 record close. Record quarters drove the climb, and worries about AI spending, sparked partly by Lam Research’s outlook, drove the fall, with no bad news from Applied itself.
